claims.text: Overall wear resistance of the FeNiCrCoCu coating at high temperature is governed by the stability and distribution of nanoscale precipitates formed during thermal exposure.
Microscopic deformation of the FeNiCrCoCu coating during high-temperature sliding is governed by the stability and distribution of nanoscale precipitates.
Thermal aging at 800°C for 24 hours will promote nanoscale precipitate formation in the coating.
Thermal aging at 800°C for 24 hours will stabilize nanoscale precipitates in the coating.
The nanoscale precipitates induced by thermal aging pin dislocations.
Precipitate-mediated dislocation pinning reduces plastic deformation during sliding.
Thermally induced nanoscale precipitates increase coating hardness.
Thermally induced nanoscale precipitates limit the generation of wear particles during sliding.
Limiting wear-particle generation increases the wear resistance of the coating.
Compared with the as-deposited coating, the thermally aged coating will have a lower wear rate during sliding at 700°C to 900°C.
Compared with the as-deposited coating, the thermally aged coating will exhibit less microscopic deformation during sliding at 700°C to 900°C.
